contexts: eight hospitals of one regional health authority
low-risk ambulatory surgery: cataract, hernia, arthroscopy
reading: Low-value testing persists mostly through defaults and habit rather than ignorance of the guidance. The retrieved evidence places the strongest levers in the ordering system (c2, c5) and in feedback on clinicians' own ordering (c1), with nurse-led triage as a clinic-level option. Education alone fades (c4). The committee's worry about cancellations and harm has some reassuring evidence (c3) but thin reporting. Patients are largely willing to go without tests when the reason is explained.

summary: Map of the ordering system, the strategies that change it and the balancing outcomes.
